methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series B → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.9x) to $100M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Transportation (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 3 same-sector peers exist in Transportation, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Arc Boats is a Series B transportation company founded by Mitch Lee and Ryan Cook that has raised over $100M to date. The transportation sector peer set comprises seven private companies, including Rivian, The Boring Company, Einride, Parallel Systems, and DeepDrive; no public comparables exist. The narrow peer set lacks sufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage transactions to support a reliable peer-median approach.

Stage-progression methodology is the primary applicable valuation lens. Using the company's $100M total raised as a baseline proxy and applying a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B progression yields an implied post-money valuation of $190M. This method assumes Arc Boats' growth trajectory aligns with median venture-backed transportation companies advancing from seed/early stages through Series B.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $162M to $218M, centered on a $190M median. The low-end estimate reflects downside assumption variance, while the high-end incorporates upside scenarios within the 1.9x multiplier framework. Key uncertainties include the stability of stage-progression multiples in early-stage transportation (where exit outcomes remain concentrated and outcome dispersion is high), the representativeness of $100M raised as a post-money proxy, and the absence of comparable company data for precise peer anchoring. Given the single-method foundation, outcomes should be stress-tested against market conditions and capital availability trends in transportation venture funding.
